slides.0.title: Kremstal, Kamptal and Traisental
slides.0.subtitle: Grüner and Riesling on the Danube's tributaries
slides.1.title: Shared rules of the three DACs
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.0.content: All three DACs allow only Grüner Veltliner and Riesling (dry)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Klassik and Reserve
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Klassik at least 12% abv, Reserve at least 13% abv
slides.1.highlights.2.title: DAC years
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Traisental 2006 and Kamptal 2008; sources give both 2006 and 2007 for Kremstal (kept out of the quiz)
slides.1.content: All three are Grüner/Riesling regions; they differ in terroir and style.
slides.2.title: Style and well-known Rieden
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Kamptal
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Often seen as strong in both Riesling and Grüner; well-known sites include Heiligenstein and Gaisberg
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Kremstal
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Centred on Krems and Stein; well-known sites include Steiner Hund and Pfaffenberg
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Traisental
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The smallest of the three and cooler, with wines often tight and mineral
slides.2.content: This page is general description, not individually verified; exam answers should rest on the DAC rules (varieties and thresholds).
Which varieties does Kamptal DAC allow?
Kamptal, Kremstal and Traisental all limit to Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
What is the minimum alcohol for Reserve in these three DACs?
Klassik is at least 12% and Reserve at least 13%.
From which vintage is Traisental DAC?
Traisental DAC dates from the 2006 vintage.
